title: Overflow axes and clipping
learningObjectives: Explain overflow axes and clipping and use the relevant layout or responsive features.

understand.concept: overflow-x and overflow-y control overflow independently on the horizontal and vertical axes. Values include visible, hidden, clip, scroll, and auto. The overflow:clip value clips content without creating a scroll container, unlike hidden in important scrolling and programmatic behaviours.
understand.whyItMatters: Clipping can hide content, focus rings, or controls. Test long words, keyboard focus, and zoom. Choose scrolling where content must remain reachable, and use clipping only when loss of access is intentional and safe.
understand.analogy: Overflow axes are two directions in which content may extend beyond its container; clipping draws a boundary around what is visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual scroll, sizing, and media-query behaviour follows browser layout rules.

explain.narrative: The horizontal axis scrolls while vertical overflow is clipped. Try overflow-x:clip and compare the scrolling behaviour.

examples.code: A deliberately long line of content that extends beyond the available width.
examples.explanation: The horizontal axis scrolls while vertical overflow is clipped. Try overflow-x:clip and compare the scrolling behaviour.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example demonstrating the lesson concept.

practise.guidedTask: Create a horizontal code sample that can be scrolled on narrow screens. Keep all content reachable by keyboard and touch.
practise.independentTask: Create a practical example and test it with longer content, keyboard interaction, and more than one viewport size.
hints: Inspect the nearest scroll container and containing block.
Test horizontal overflow and keyboard reachability.

questions.prompt: Which value clips overflow without creating a scroll container?
questions.explanation: overflow:clip clips content and does not create a scroll container.
